prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout of the room across the camera wearer's movement: in frames 1 to 3, the camera wearer approaches an open doorway ahead (~1.5–3 m away) while a high wooden desk and lower bench sit within arm's reach (~0.4–1 m) on the right, and in frames 4 to 5 the wearer turns right so the desk and wall shift to the left foreground (~0.3–1 m) and recede up to ~3.5 m toward the back of the room. In frame 2, two water jugs are faintly visible on the floor to the left (~2.5 m away, ~1.5 m left of the bench), and in frame 5 a man stands on the right (~2–2.5 m from the camera wearer) facing toward the camera with his extended right hand touching the desk edge within his reach and his lower legs partly occluded by the bench below. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map clearly separates the receding planar geometry of the upper desk surface from the lower bench and isolates the standing man's silhouette in frame 5 from the cluttered background cabinets (~4–5 m behind him). However, the depth map is unreliable in the brightly lit doorway of frames 2 and 3—rendering the opening as pitch black with no exterior surface structure—and fails to distinguish the partially visible person entering the far right edge of frame 4.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map detects regions only in frames 1, 2, and 5, leaving frames 3 and 4 completely blank as the camera wearer walks toward the doorway and turns right. In frame 1, a purple mask labeled 'dining table' outlines the wooden desk extending from within the camera wearer's arm's reach (~0.5 m) on the bottom right to ~2.5 m ahead, while in frame 2 a large green 'laptop' mask covers the left wall, blackboard, and water jugs (~2–3.5 m away). In frame 5, after the camera turns right, a pink 'bed' mask covers the foreground desk and bench on the left (~0.3–2.5 m away), a pink 'person' mask (with a tan 'cell phone' mask on his head) outlines the man standing ~2–2.5 m away on the right who faces and looks toward the camera wearer with his right hand reaching the desk edge, and a magenta 'tv' mask covers the upper background cabinets (~4 m away, behind and above him). While the frame 5 masks help delineate the boundary where the foreground bench occludes the man's lower legs, the map provides little spatial insight beyond the RGB image and is highly unreliable due to severe class mislabeling across all frames and total detection failure in frames 3 and 4 (including missing the person partly visible at the right edge of frame 4).
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely empty in frames 1 through 4 and renders a single yellow body skeleton in frame 5 for the man standing on the right (~2–2.5 m from the camera wearer) after the camera wearer turns away from the doorway toward the back of the room. The frame 5 skeleton shows his facial keypoints (nose, eyes, and ears) and torso oriented toward the camera wearer and slightly to the left, with his right arm extended outward so his right wrist sits within arm's reach at the edge of the wooden desk (~2.5 m from the camera) and his left arm angled down toward his hip. His lower-body keypoints cut off at the hips and upper thighs, reflecting the occlusion of his lower legs behind the wooden bench and the bottom edge of the frame. Compared to the dimly lit RGB frame, the skeleton makes the exact angles of his shoulders, elbows, and head orientation immediately clear, but the map is unreliable in omitting all magenta hand keypoints and failing to detect the man's head and shoulder when he first appears partially in view at the far right edge of frame 4.
